title: Designs that other teams must live with
summary: A boundary is a contract and an operating responsibility, not just a box.

steps.title: A shared API changes under three teams
steps.text: Your team renames a response field. The website updates, but a billing job and an old mobile client fail overnight. The data shape was an informal contract even though nobody wrote it down. A design crosses team boundaries whenever another team must depend on its behavior, availability or change schedule.

steps.title: Put authority with an owner
steps.text: Change a required API field and watch consumer contracts break. Keep v1, let measured usage fall as consumers migrate, then choose when to retire it.

steps.title: Worked example: the on-call bill
steps.text: An operating model constrains delivery even when the infrastructure bill is small. Combining services does not automatically remove pages; eliminating repeated failure paths or clarifying ownership may help. The last callers in an API migration can include the least observable batch jobs. This is an operating worksheet, not a simulated page count.

diagram.label: Count the operating bill
parts: 8 × 45 minutes × 52 weeks. Three operators still need delivery time.
180 of 200 migrated. Identify the last batch jobs before retiring the old API.

rows.label: Remaining callers
rows.how: 200 - 180; risk depends on which callers remain

steps.q: Three teams write one table and each assumes another owns recovery. What must their contract establish?
choices: A shared on-call channel with no authority to settle conflicting writes
Allowed writers, invariant enforcement, recovery owner and change rules
One API schema while leaving direct table writes unrestricted
steps.why: A communication channel and schema are useful, but do not assign data authority or recovery decisions.

steps.q: Where would you split this service? Follow-up: another team needs to change independently.
checklist: Map writes that must commit together and assign their authority
Explain whether an API boundary can preserve the invariant
Assign versioning, dependency-failure behavior and recovery ownership
steps.model: I would first map the writes that must commit together and who can operate them. A separate team can own a coherent capability through an API without directly mutating another team's tables. If that boundary splits an invariant, we need a redesigned workflow or must keep the transaction together. I would document data authority, versioning, failure behavior and on-call before treating independent deployment as a benefit. A module boundary may be enough until the operating case is clear.

steps.title: Write a document people can disagree with
steps.text: Start a design document with user promises, non-goals and measured constraints. Show the request path, data owner and invariant, then alternatives, failure cases, cost and open questions. Ask reviewers to challenge one decision. Prefer additive changes and explicit versions for incompatible meaning. Publish deprecation dates, contact consumers and agree exception policies. A quiet dashboard cannot prove that an annual caller has migrated.

diagram.label: A contract needs evidence
parts: Fields, errors, freshness, deletion and compatibility need explicit semantics.
Instrument caller identities. An annual job may be absent from a quiet dashboard.
Offer migration paths, contact owners and test old clients before removal.

steps.q: Ninety percent of callers migrated to a new API. What evidence supports removing the old endpoint?
choices: No calls appeared in the last month, even though annual jobs exist
The website and newest mobile app pass their tests
Remaining callers are identified and migrated or covered by an agreed exception policy
steps.why: Important infrequent or older consumers can remain after the most visible clients migrate.

steps.q: How will you deprecate an API used by teams you do not know? Follow-up: one annual caller never appears in the last month's logs.
checklist: Inventory caller identities through credentials, code and owners
Publish a replacement, support window and owner-tested migration
Account for annual jobs and record exceptions before removal
steps.model: I would inventory consumers from credentials, code references, owners and telemetry, then publish the replacement and a support window. Usage logs are evidence, but a month misses annual jobs. I would ask identified owners to test the replacement and check schedules, run a controlled warning phase and keep an explicit exception owner. Removal needs a decision about the remaining risk. I would record that decision so a future on-call engineer does not have to reconstruct it during an outage.

steps.q: Two actions share a required local transaction invariant and one operating team. What is a reasonable initial boundary?
choices: One cohesive module or service that commits the invariant locally
Separate services with compensations assumed to preserve the same atomic visibility
Separate services that each update their own row without a shared decision
steps.why: Splitting the writes changes failure and visibility semantics. Keep the transaction local unless another requirement warrants redesigning it.

takeaway: Name the invariant, the owner and the compatibility promise before drawing a team boundary.
